payload.speaker: Xavi
payload.text: Friends, I arrived early at the square and noticed Cyrus kept glancing at the harbor bell before anyone spoke. Small things, like a dog that doesn't bark. I'm not ready to point at anyone yet. I'd rather we listen closely today and see who hurries to fill the silence.

payload.speaker: Cyrus
payload.text: Ah, Xavi, the Dog-That-Didn't-Bark. I checked the harbor bell because I've rung one for thirty years, and a bell that's sulking is worth a glance. Mind you, that's a habit, not a confession. Tess is "Crumb" to me, since she's always got flour on her. I'll be watching who rushes to fill silences, and Iris, you're very quick to chair this meeting, Mayor.

payload.speaker: Zane
payload.text: Easy now, friends. Gulls are circling low over the harbor and the tide's gone sour, and in my experience that's an omen for somebody on this square. I won't sink a finger on a bell-glance. Cyrus, you were quick to explain that bell. Iris, you were quick to chair. Quick isn't guilty, but I'll be watching the hands that hurry. I'm listening before I cast a line.

payload.speaker: Umar
payload.text: Point by point, friends. Cyrus explained the harbor bell before anyone asked, then leaned on Tess with a pet name to shift our eyes. That's deflection, not proof. Iris chairing is her duty as mayor, so I won't hold it against her. Xavi, I'd like to hear more evidence before we settle on anyone, and Cyrus, I'd like your reason for the bell.

payload.speaker: Iris
payload.text: Order, friends! I propose a motion: every Resident states one fact they saw this morning, and we hold our vote only after all have spoken. Cyrus, your bell-glance is a fair question, and I'd like your answer plainly. Umar makes a sound point about deflection. I chair only because someone must, and I'm happy to be questioned.

payload.speaker: Wren
payload.text: Good morning, neighbours! Wren here, carpenter, so I build my case one plank at a time. Cyrus, you explained the harbor bell before anyone asked, then nudged Tess into the spotlight with a pet name. That's a loose joint worth checking. I'm not nailing anyone yet. *knocks on wood* Let's gather more boards before we hammer.

Let's not spoil the dough by rushing to a verdict on Day One.
